signals.topic: GPT-5.x /responses endpoint silently hangs 10-28% of concurrent requests with no error or retry
signals.summary: Under moderate concurrent load (5 simultaneous calls), the /v1/responses endpoint silently drops 10-28% of requests. Affected requests receive no HTTP error, no timeout, no retry — TCP connection hangs indefinitely until the caller kills it. Both raw AsyncOpenAI and Agents SDK Runner.run() are affected at the same rate, confirming this is an OpenAI API server-side issue. The SDK cannot retry because no error is received.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：10-28%并发请求静默挂起，用户无法感知失败（无错误码/无超时），SDK无法自动重试，因为根本没收到错误响应。实测数据（4轮×50次调用）显示持续复现，平均延迟高达3-4秒才挂起。虽issue自述'非SDK问题'，但直接阻断Agents SDK用户的实际使用，是真实的高影响用户痛点。

source_issues.title: GPT-5.1 / GPT-5.4 /responses endpoint silently hangs 10-28% of concurrent requests
source_issues.evidence: 10-28% of concurrent requests hang with no error, no timeout, no retry. Reproduced across 4 test runs with 50 calls each. Both raw AsyncOpenAI and Agents SDK hang at the same rate (20% vs 24%). TCP handshake completes but no HTTP response ever returned.

signals.topic: Preambles/commentary messages disappear when structured output (output_type) is enabled

This creates a UX 'dead zone' where nothing is streamed to the user while tools execute. The preamble is documented as a latency-reduction feature — without it, users see a blank screen with no acknowledgment during tool execution.

signals.topic: Traces are silently dropped in long-running workers (Celery, FastAPI background tasks) without any warning

Long-running workers (Celery, FastAPI background tasks, RQ, Dramatiq) never shut down, causing traces to remain buffered forever and never appear on platform.openai.com/traces. No error or warning is emitted, making this extremely hard to diagnose. The user provided a working 3-line fix.

tracing silent failure in production workers

signals.topic: Turbo fails to start on Windows when installed via Bun (spawnSync UNKNOWN error)
signals.summary: When turbo is installed globally via Bun on Windows, any `turbo run build` or `turbo info` command crashes with spawnSync UNKNOWN error, making the entire build pipeline unusable. Windows security also blocks turbo.exe loading.
signals.review_reason: Critical functionality completely blocked on Windows+Bun: turbo crashes on every invocation with spawnSync UNKNOWN error. Users cannot run builds at all. Windows security actively blocks turbo.exe from loading. This is a primary platform failure, not an edge case.

source_issues.title: Bun run build failed on window on fresh turbo repo

Windows security pops up: 'Part of this app has been blocked — Some features of Node.js JavaScript Runtime may not work because we can't confirm who published turbo.exe'. Multiple workaround attempts (global bun install, deleting node_modules) all failed.

signals.topic: turbo prune --docker corrupts bun.lock with phantom npm packages (v2.8.16+ regression)
signals.summary: Running `turbo prune --docker` on a bun monorepo produces a corrupted bun.lock file that injects ~700 phantom npm internal packages (@npmcli/*, @sigstore/*, cacache, libnpm*) not present in the original. `bun install --frozen-lockfile` then fails, breaking CI/CD docker image builds.
aliases: prune docker bun frozen lockfile fails
signals.review_reason: Docker prune workflow completely broken for bun monorepos. This is a core CI/CD use case — generating lean docker images from monorepos. The pruned lockfile fails frozen lockfile validation, forcing users to either skip validation or pin to v2.8.15. Clear regression introduced by PR #12228.

source_issues.title: turbo prune --docker injects phantom npm packages into bun.lock (v2.8.16 regression from #12228)
source_issues.evidence: Regression from PR #12228. Diff shows ~700 phantom entries added to bun.lock (npm internals like @gar/promise-retry, @npmcli/agent, @sigstore/*, cacache, libnpm*). `bun install --frozen-lockfile` rejects the pruned output with 'lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen'. v2.8.15 works, v2.8.16+ broken. Workaround: pin to v2.8.15.

signals.topic: Dirty .gitignore breaks turbo caching by leaking gitignored files into task input hashes (v2.8.18+ regression)
signals.summary: When .gitignore has any uncommitted modification, turbo v2.8.18+ stops respecting .gitignore patterns during task input hashing. node_modules/ and other gitignored files leak into input hashes, permanently busting the cache. In large monorepos this also causes turbo to walk hundreds of thousands of files on every invocation.
aliases: gitignored files in task hashes regression v2.8.18
signals.review_reason: Regression that silently breaks the core value proposition of turbo — incremental caching. Any developer who modifies .gitignore during a workflow (very common) loses all cache effectiveness. In large monorepos, it also triggers expensive file system walks of node_modules/ on every invocation. Not P0 because it requires an uncommitted .gitignore modification to trigger.

source_issues.title: Dirty .gitignore causes gitignored files to leak into task input hashes (v2.8.18+)
source_issues.evidence: Regression from v2.8.18 (introduced by #12339). Clean .gitignore: 4 inputs, 0 leaking. Dirty .gitignore: 5 inputs, 1 leaking (node_modules/.bin/foo). v2.8.17 correctly handles both. Cache permanently broken while .gitignore is dirty. Modifying .gitignore before committing is a normal workflow — silently breaks all caching until change is committed.

signals.topic: Turbo executes unnecessary tasks for packages that don't define the requested task script
signals.summary: When running `turbo run test`, turbo builds a task graph assuming all packages contain the requested task. Packages without the task are still included, causing unnecessary build tasks to run. Only packages actually defining the task should be considered when building the graph.
aliases: task graph includes packages without task script
signals.review_reason: Long-standing ergonomics issue (open since 2022) causing wasted CI time by running tasks for packages that don't need them. Not a full block but wastes compute. Lower priority because it doesn't prevent the build from succeeding, only runs extra unnecessary work. No recent escalation despite age.

source_issues.title: Scripts are run unnecessarily depending on how turbo is configured

The `build` task of unrelated packages runs unnecessarily. Issue open since March 2022 with 52 comments, never resolved.

signals.topic: CLI `vc link` links to wrong project causing deployments to go to incorrect target

This is a deployment target confusion that silently misroutes work.
signals.review_reason: This is a concrete deployment target confusion that silently misroutes work. This is an active-flow failure (wrong project gets deployed) with clear reproduction steps and no workaround. Count=1 but severity is high since the user cannot deploy to the intended project at all.

signals.topic: Go build with vendored dependencies fails because Vercel ignores vendor directory and attempts to download private packages
signals.summary: When deploying a Go project that uses `go mod vendor`, Vercel's build process ignores the vendored dependencies and runs `go mod tidy`, which attempts to download private repository dependencies. Since the Vercel builder environment does not have access to those private repos, the build fails. Setting `-mod=vendor` via GO_BUILD_FLAGS or UI environment variables does not resolve the issue.
signals.review_reason: Go vendored dependency builds are completely blocked with no effective workaround. The build command runs `go mod tidy` which attempts private repo access the builder doesn't have, causing a hard build failure. User-documented workarounds (GO_BUILD_FLAGS, UI env vars) do not work. This is a workflow runtime failure affecting Go monorepo users with private dependencies.

source_issues.title: Can't get vercel to deploy a go mod vendor-ed project

Build process does not check for vendor/modules.txt to use vendor mode automatically.
